title: The Tally of Dishonor
sourceBasis: THE HOARD OF CHASE BANK teleplay inventory
enhancementDecision: Preserve the existing 24-page production script rather than replace it. It is already the prior full enhancement pass and contains the required bank escalation, Gunnar route intelligence, and toaster payoff. The current pass locks its causal structure and corrects the surrounding season description so unrelated reputation/Yelp language does not overwrite the approved bank story.
issueFunction: Financial legibility as a modern form of status and participation. Bjorn must become recognizable to a bank without surrendering his own understanding of value; Carrie translates him into acceptable documents; Gunnar reads the institution and city as systems; the accepted metal/toaster logic turns an absurd promotional object into a concrete sign that the group has gained partial civic agency.
causalSpine: The provisional-status deadline forces the bank trip.
The bank converts identity, address, value, and access into procedural gates.
Carrie repeatedly translates DTI reality into ordinary bank requirements rather than merely explaining jokes.
Gunnar maps routes, exits, transactions, and weaknesses; his system-reading must materially help the group progress.
Bjorn rejects abstract or hollow status objects but responds to tangible value and obligation.
The promotional metal/toaster negotiation is the earned resolution of the value conflict, not a detachable gag.
Completed paperwork leaves the Vikings more administratively legible and less dependent than when they entered.

characterLocks.Bjorn: Sovereignty and provision remain the emotional problem. He is not confused because he is stupid; he objects when modern value is intangible, revocable, or dependent on another institution's permission.
characterLocks.Carrie: Her competence drives the institutional victory. She understands which documents, wording, exceptions, and human decisions can make the bank accept an impossible customer.
characterLocks.Gunnar: His mapping is causal, not decorative. Preserve his city-navigation intelligence established in Issue 3 and show him applying the same pattern-reading to financial space and procedure.
characterLocks.bankStaff: Ordinary employees following rational procedure, not villains or buffoons. Friction comes from systems designed for ordinary contemporary customers.
characterLocks.Silas: Do not force Silas into the bank sequence unless an existing approved page already requires him. His broader progression should not steal the bank issue's causal spine.

continuityLocks: Issue 3 has already established Gunnar as capable of learning and navigating modern systems; Issue 4 must build on that competence rather than reset him.
The Bushwick apartment is already home/territory, so proof-of-address friction should feel like the system failing to recognize an established lived reality.
DTI documents are mundane municipal paperwork, not futuristic temporal technology.
New York and bank environments remain ordinary 2026 spaces with material specificity and indifferent bystanders.
Legacy S1E02 payload IDs remain stable identifiers and are not renumbered solely because the material is now Issue 4.
readerTest: A reader should be able to explain, without production notes, why they must open the account now, what blocks them, what Carrie changes, what Gunnar contributes, why Bjorn objects to the offered forms of value, why the toaster/metal object solves the emotional-comic argument, and what concrete new capability the Vikings possess when they leave.
excludedReframing: Do not turn this issue into a Yelp/reputation-system story.
Do not import BLOOD FEUD 311 merely to justify the title.
Do not dilute the bank escalation with unrelated municipal complaint material.
Do not renumber stable production IDs as a cosmetic cleanup.
